## Setting up my environment
Notes: setting up my R environment by loading ggplot2

```{r loading_packages}

library(ggplot2)

```

# Introduction

This project analyzes weekly weather data using R

### Load Data

```{r}
days <- c("Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday" , "Sunday")
temperature <- c(28, 30, 29, 31, 27, 26, 32)
rainfall <- c(5, 0, 10, 0, 2, 8, 0)

weather <- data.frame(
  days = days,
  temperature = temperature,
  rainfall = rainfall
)

print(weather)

```

### Summary Statistics

```{r}
avg_temp <- mean(temperature)
cat("Average temperature:", avg_temp, "°C\n")

highest_temp <- max(temperature)
cat("Highest temperature:", highest_temp, "°C\n")

lowest_temp <- min(temperature)
cat("Lowest temperature:", lowest_temp, "°C\n")

total_rainfall <- sum(rainfall)
cat("Total rainfall:", total_rainfall, "mm\n")

```

### Rain Analysis

```{r}
rainy_day <- sum(rainfall > 0)
cat("Rainy days:", rainy_day, "\n")

dry_day <- sum(rainfall == 0)
cat("Dry days:", dry_day, "\n")

```

### Weather category

```{r}
weather$weather_category <- ifelse(weather$temperature > 30, "Hot",
                           ifelse(weather$temperature >= 25 & weather$temperature <= 30, "Warm", 
                                  "Cool"))
print(weather)

```

### Add Visualization

```{r temperature_visualization}
ggplot(data = weather, aes(x = days, y = temperature, fill = weather_category)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  labs(title = "Weekly Temperature Report",
       x = "Day",
       y = "Temperature (°C)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

```

The highest temperature recorded was 32°C on Sunday, indicating a very hot end to the week.
